script.title: There are 15,000 city-killer asteroids we can't see
script.description: A step-by-step breakdown of the physics behind a city-killer asteroid impact and how NASA plans to stop them.

shots.narration: A city-killer asteroid hits your atmosphere in under ten seconds.
This massive rock travels at thirty thousand miles per hour.
The impact releases the force of eight million tons of TNT.
If the Sun were a basketball, this rock is a grain of sand.
Yet it carries enough energy to flatten all of Washington DC.
Surprisingly, we have only found forty percent of these hidden killers.
Fifteen thousand undetected asteroids are currently orbiting near your home.
NASA tested a plan to nuke them before they reach you.
A nuclear blast sends blistering X-rays into the asteroid's skin.
The rock vaporizes and turns into a cloud of expanding gas.
In sixty-eight milliseconds, the entire internal structure is shattered.
The debris flies away faster than the rock's own gravity.
This turns a city-killer into a harmless cloud of dust.
But until we find them, a city-killer asteroid hits in ten seconds.
